messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 streaming latency spike detected for hosted model endpoints in us-west1. Threshold breached (SLO p99 > 2s) for the last 5m, streaming stalls observed. Affected pool: shared-gpu-pool-3. Auto-escalation to incidents channel. :rotating_light:

sara-ng: seeing the alert — dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/streams/streaming-latency?orgId=1&var-region=us-west1. p95 ~ 480ms, p99 ~ 5.8s, error rate up (streaming stalls / io timeouts). Which tenants on gpu-pool-3 right now?

mike-g: running host-level checks. iostat and dmesg show repeated writeback stalls and GPU page-faults on host host-3b2. cgroup blkio counters for tenant t-42 are very high. suspect a batch checkpoint causing heavy NVMe writeback + nv_peer_memory churn.

cheng-li: tagging this as multi-tenant IO/noisy-tenant. quick mitigation options: 1) throttle t-42 cgroup blkio weight, 2) evict t-42 from shared-gpu-pool-3 to dedicated capacity (if reserved), 3) route streaming traffic to fallback model variant in another region. Which is fastest?

sara-ng: can we throttle first? eviction will cause cold starts for that tenant if we move them. need to communicate. customer-impact: 3 active customers on shared pool showing >30% of streaming requests time out after 3s. Product notified: @oncall-roster pinged.

mike-g: throttle test: running command on host: ```sudo cgset -r blkio.weight=100 /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/machine.slice/machine-qemu_t-42.service``` will reduce IO priority. also can set blkio.throttle.read_bps_device for nvme device. prepping a script to apply transient throttle across pool hosts.

ops-bot: NOTE: Runbook referenced: https://wiki.redwood/incident/runbooks/noisy-tenant-eviction. Recommended first step: apply cgroup throttle for suspected tenant for 5 minutes and monitor p99.

cheng-li: assigning ops to apply throttle on host-3b2 now. sara/mike monitor metrics and errors. If no improvement in 120s, proceed to evacuation plan. I will prepare the migration plan.

mike-g: throttle applied on host-3b2. p99 dropped from 5.8s -> 2.1s in the first minute. streaming stalls reduced but still above SLO. digging into KV cache evictions — we see high KV miss rate for streaming path which adds extra RPCs.

sara-ng: good improvement. can we roll throttle across other hosts in pool? also start notifying affected customers: team-sla-alerts will send status page update. message draft: "We are investigating elevated latency for streaming features in us-west1; mitigation in progress."

cheng-li: rolling throttle to other hosts with the same pattern. simultaneously starting evacuation of tenant t-42 to dedicated-reserve-7. migration will be live-move (detach volumes, reattach) — expect ~60-90s disruption for that tenant.

mike-g: during migration we see a short burst of 502s for a small subset of streams (~0.8% errors) aligned with volume detach. overall p99 now ~1.4s post-eviction on hosts that had throttles + migration started.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Mitigation in progress. Eviction started for tenant t-42 -> dedicated-reserve-7. SLO trend: p99 trending down. No customer-facing outage declared yet; degraded performance only.

oncall-roster: handing off to night on-call: @cheng-li please take the on-call handoff — you're now main incident owner. Include timeline and actions in channel.

cheng-li: taking handoff. summary: root cause candidate = tenant t-42 large checkpoint writes triggering NVMe writeback + kernel IO contention, causing GPU page-fault latency amplifications for co-tenants. Live steps taken: applied cgroup blkio throttles to reduce priority, evicted/migrated t-42 to dedicated-reserve-7, applied temporary routing fallback for streaming traffic to us-west2 for critical routes.

sara-ng: customer impact notes: 3 paying customers saw elevated latency, one reported UI stalls. CS notified, will open support tickets and attach timeline and mitigation steps.

mike-g: logs snippet: ```[kern] pid=9876 writeback: writeback start dev nvme0n1 queue 512ms```. Also NVMe SMART for host-3b2 shows high contended latency; will schedule deeper hardware checks post-incident.

cheng-li: action items post-mitigation: 1) postmortem + RCA, 2) add automatic detection for sustained blkio spikes per-tenant, 3) implement soft-eviction policy in runtime to preemptively isolate tenants before p99 breaches, 4) update capacity planner to avoid placing batch-heavy tenants on shared streaming pools.

sara-ng: closing note: p99 in us-west1 down to 0.9s, error rate back to baseline. marking incident as mitigated but keeping channel open for 2h for monitoring. Please add any logs/traces to the incident thread. :white_check_mark:

mike-g: copying key logs to incident storage: s3://redwood-incidents/1755509876/logs.tar.gz. Will follow up with kernel traces and NVMe metrics.

ops-bot: REMINDER: runbook requires customer comms template + postmortem within 72h.

cheng-li: will draft postmortem and assign owners. moving to postmortem label and closing on-call handoff. thanks everyone for quick response. :bow:
